newsitem.title: KAZAKHSTAN: Uighurs arrested in China on bomb charges - exiles.
newsitem.headline: Uighurs arrested in China on bomb charges - exiles.

text.p: Chinese police have arrested at least 20 ethnic Uighurs suspected of carrying out bombings in China's northern province of Xinjiang, an exiled nationalist Uighur leader said on Thursday.

"A witness who came yesterday from Xinjiang said the police are hunting for suspects in Uighur quarters of the towns of Urumqi and Yining," Kakharman Khozhamberdi, head of a local Uighur association, told Reuters in the Kazakh capital Almaty.
"At least 20 ethnic Uighurs have been arrested...but the real number may be even higher because we have no information whether new arrests took place last night," he added.
On February 25 Xinjiang's capital Urumqi was shattered by a series of three deadly bombings. The explosions took place on the day Beijing held funeral rites for late leader Deng Xiaoping.
Chinese officials said nine people were killed and 74 wounded in the bombings organised by Uighur nationalists.
Exiled Uighur nationalists in Kazakhstan have said there had been another "blast of revenge for atrocities done by the Chinese to ethnic Uighurs on Monday" but Chinese officials denied this.
Moslem separatists say they want to set up an independent "East Turkestan" in Xinjiang, home to many Turkic-speaking people such as the Uighurs.

In February, an anti-Chinese riot by local Uighurs, one of the largest and most violent since the 1949 communist takeover, broke out in Yining. Chinese officials said nine people were killed in the riot, while Uighur leaders said around 100 of their kinsmen had lost their lives.
Khozhamberdi said the police were torturing those detained.
"Special-purpose units have been sent to the (northern) province of Xinjiang from central parts of China to reinforce local police forces," he said.

"But our kinsmen stoutly resist repressions. There have been several clashes across Xinjiang. In Tukhu Yuzi village, near Yining, two policemen were killed several days ago as they tried to arrest a local boy of Uighur nationality," Khozhamberdi said.
